questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: What is the recommended dimensional data model shape for performant Power BI datasets?

options.text: One giant flattened denormalized CSV with 150 columns
Deep multi-hop snowflake chains with bidirectional many-to-many links
Completely unlinked isolated tables queried via MERGE in visuals
Star Schema: central Fact table containing numeric transactions linked via 1-to-many relationships to Dimension lookup tables

questions.explanation: Star schemas optimize VertiPaq columnar compression, minimize ambiguous filter paths, and simplify DAX measures.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Power BI

questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: When should you author a DAX Measure rather than a Calculated Column?

options.text: Measures consume triple the disk storage of columns
Calculated columns re-evaluate whenever slicers are clicked
For dynamic aggregations, ratios, and YoY KPIs evaluated at query time within active report filter context without bloating RAM
When placing static grouping labels inside visual X-axis slicers

questions.explanation: Measures compute dynamically using filter context with zero static RAM overhead, whereas calculated columns compute on data refresh and persist per row.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Power BI

questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: Which DAX function safely computes ratios without raising `#DIV/0!` infinity errors when the denominator is zero or blank?

options.text: AVERAGEIF()
DIVIDE(numerator, denominator, alternateResult)
QUOTIENT_SAFE()
Standard `/` operator

questions.explanation: `DIVIDE()` cleanly guards against zero denominators and defaults to `BLANK()` or an explicit fallback.

questions.prompt: What is the only DAX function capable of modifying or overriding active visual filter context cleanly?

options.text: SUMX()
RELATED()
FORMAT()
CALCULATE(<expression>, <filter1>, ...)

questions.prompt: In Power Query, what does 'Query Folding' optimize?

options.text: Merging all report pages into a single visual
Translating M transformations into native SQL pushed down directly to the source database rather than pulling raw unfiltered rows into Power BI
Compressing visual PNG screenshots inside PBIX archives
Collapsing DAX nested IF blocks into one line

questions.prompt: Why should high-cardinality text columns (like millisecond transaction UUIDs or unparsed timestamps) be split or removed unless strictly needed?

options.text: High unique value counts undermine VertiPaq dictionary compression and inflate model RAM memory footprint
Power BI refuses to load any string longer than 5 characters
UUIDs cause negative totals in SUM measures
High cardinality disables dark mode themes

questions.explanation: VertiPaq column-store compression excels on low-cardinality columns; dropping unused high-cardinality IDs keeps models fast and small.

questions.prompt: What does Dynamic Row-Level Security (RLS) use in DAX roles so one rule adapts to every logged-in viewer?

options.text: Hardcoding 500 static user email filters manually
Hiding visual headers with white rectangles
Applying page filters manually before PDF export
`[EmployeeEmail] = USERPRINCIPALNAME()`

questions.explanation: `USERPRINCIPALNAME()` resolves the signed-in Power BI Service viewer identity dynamically inside RLS filter expressions.

questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: In relationship cardinality, which direction flows naturally from Dimension lookup tables down to Fact tables in a clean Star Schema?

options.text: Many-to-Many unindexed joins across all tables
Fact -> Dimension reverse filtering only
Single-directional (One-to-Many: Dimension -> Fact)
Bidirectional everywhere by default

questions.explanation: Single-direction filtering from Dimensions to Facts avoids circular ambiguity and maximizes query speed.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Power BI

questions.prompt: A `Total Sales All Regions = CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALL(Regions))` card shows a number, yet adding `Regions[Country]` to a table causes every row to repeat the grand total. Why?

options.text: ALL() multiplies metrics by the number of rows
Table visuals ignore CALCULATE
Total Sales needs SUMX around ALL()
`ALL(Regions)` explicitly removes all visual filter context on the Regions table, yielding the unfiltered grand total per row

questions.explanation: `ALL()` ignores filters on the specified table—which is precisely how denominator percentages (`% of Total`) are computed cleanly.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Power BI

questions.prompt: A developer notices `SUM(Sales[Quantity] * Sales[UnitPrice])` throws a DAX syntax error inside a Measure. Why?

options.text: Measures cannot reference two columns in the same table
Parentheses are forbidden inside SUM
`SUM` aggregates a single column only; row-by-row multiplication inside a measure requires the iterator `SUMX(Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[UnitPrice])`
DAX cannot multiply currency columns

questions.explanation: Aggregators like `SUM` lack row context; X-suffix iterators (`SUMX`, `AVERAGEX`) step row-by-row over a table.

questions.prompt: Two Fact tables (`Sales` and `Targets`) both link to `DimDate` and `DimRegion`. Enabling bidirectional filters everywhere throws an 'ambiguous path' model error. How do you fix this?

options.text: Turn all Fact columns into text fields
Keep Star Schema relationships single-directional (Dimension -> both Fact tables) instead of bidirectional cross-filtering
Merge `Sales` and `Targets` into one table with null padding
Delete `DimDate` entirely

questions.explanation: Single-directional filtering from shared conformed Dimensions resolves multi-fact ambiguity cleanly.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Power BI

questions.prompt: Your report's YTD line chart displays empty blanks beyond March even though raw data exists in April. Inspecting `DimDate` shows missing weekends/holidays in April. Why?

options.text: Time Intelligence functions require a contiguous Date table containing every calendar day without skipped dates
DAX only aggregates the first 90 days of any calendar year
Line charts cannot render dates past Q1
Weekends are excluded automatically by Power BI Desktop

questions.explanation: A Date table generated via `CALENDAR(MIN, MAX)` guarantees continuous dates with zero gaps.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Power BI

questions.prompt: A Power Query merge query loads fast on small files, yet refreshing SQL Server data pulls 20 million rows slowly across the network. Inspecting M steps reveals `Table.Buffer` early in the query. Why?

options.text: SQL Server forbids MERGE queries over TCP
Unpivoting columns multiplies network bytes
Power Query strips WHERE filters deliberately after 1M rows
Non-foldable M steps like `Table.Buffer` early in a query break Query Folding, forcing local evaluation instead of native SQL pushdown

questions.explanation: Keep foldable operations (`SelectColumns`, `Filter`, `Group`) first before custom non-foldable M functions so the DB does the heavy lifting.

questions.prompt: You need an executive metric showing `% Share of Regional Sales` that updates dynamically when filtering years via slicer. Which DAX expression works correctly?

options.text: `[Total Sales] / [Total Sales]`
`SUM(Sales[Amount]) / COUNTROWS(Sales)`
`RELATED(Regions[Share])`
`DIVIDE([Total Sales], CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALLSELECTED(Regions)))`

questions.explanation: `ALLSELECTED` clears inner visual row filters while respecting external page/report slicers.

questions.prompt: Sales rows contain both `OrderDate` and `ShipDate`. Both must slice cleanly by calendar months inside one report. How do you model this cleanly?

options.text: Store dates purely as formatted strings without relationships
Delete ShipDate from the dataset
Create one active relationship (`OrderDate -> DimDate`) and one inactive relationship (`ShipDate -> DimDate`), activating ShipDate per measure via `USERELATIONSHIP()`
Turn both relationships active simultaneously (forbidden in DAX)

questions.explanation: Role-playing dimensions use `USERELATIONSHIP(Fact[ShipDate], DimDate[Date])` cleanly inside `CALCULATE()`.

questions.prompt: A complex measure computes `[Total Sales]` four times inside nested `IF` statements, slowing visuals down. What DAX syntax cleans readability and avoids redundant re-evaluation?

options.text: Use Calculated Columns per visual
Store `[Total Sales]` once in a `VAR` declaration before `RETURN` so the engine caches and reuses its result
Duplicate `[Total Sales]` into 4 separate measures
Replace `[Total Sales]` with `CALCULATETABLE`

questions.explanation: `VAR ... RETURN` captures the result inside its filter context once, eliminating repeated evaluation passes.

`UserEmail` and `Department`
`MinRows` and `MaxPages`
`ExportCSV` and `ThemeMode`

questions.prompt: Your report compares Budget (at monthly granularity) against Daily Sales (at daily granularity). How should you prevent users from misinterpreting daily Budget projections?

options.text: Duplicate full monthly budgets onto every single day row (multiplying totals 30x)
Join FactSales directly to FactBudget Many-to-Many
Disable all visual tooltips
Model Budget to a Month-start key or use DAX `ISINSCOPE(DimDate[Date])` to suppress meaningless daily budget breakdowns

questions.explanation: Handling multi-grain fact tables safely prevents silent 30x double-counting when drilling down below the budget grain.

questions.prompt: Author a DAX measure computing Year-over-Year (YoY) Revenue growth percentage safely:

options.text: ([Total Rev] - [Total Rev]) / 'Date'[Year]
SUMX(SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]), [Total Rev])
AVERAGE(Sales[Rev]) * 100
VAR Cur = [Total Rev] VAR Prev = CALCULATE([Total Rev], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) RETURN DIVIDE(Cur - Prev, Prev)

questions.explanation: `SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR` shifts the contiguous Date filter context back 1 year, and `DIVIDE` prevents zero-division errors.

Write 12 separate DAX `SUM` measures hardcoded per month
